rows.supplied_statement: An elementary quotient of the homotopy category. Let $\mathscr K$ be the homotopy category of CW homotopy types, and fix $K=S^1$. Let $I(X,Y)$ be the set of homotopy classes $X\to Y$ factoring through $K$. There is a category $\mathscr Q$ with the same objects and \[ \mathscr Q(X,Y)=\bigl(\mathscr K(X,Y)\amalg\{0\}\bigr)/ \bigl(I(X,Y)\sim0\bigr). \] For the quotient functor $q:\mathscr K\to\mathscr Q$, the morphism $q(f)$ is invertible exactly when $f$ is invertible in $\mathscr K$, or both its source and target are homotopy retracts of $S^1$. Those retracts have homotopy type $e$ or $S^1$.

B.17 refutes several of the other nontriviality equivalences under the literal absolute axioms. Replacing absolute Loc~(3) in D\'efinition~1.1 by relative Loc~(3 bis) repairs the product argument in B.8; the separate correction in B.11 is still needed. Optional axioms Loc~(4)--(8) retain their stated hypotheses.

rows.supplied_statement: Trivial monodromy is necessary and sufficient for integral and rational homology. Let $p:E\to B$ be a categorical covering, that is, a discrete fibration and discrete opfibration. For either $k=\mathbb Z$ or $k=\mathbb Q$, it belongs to $\Fib_{W_{Hk}}$ if and only if its monodromy on every fibre set is trivial. Equivalently, over each connected component $B_0$ it is isomorphic to a product $B_0\times S_0\to B_0$, where $S_0$ may be empty or infinite. In particular a nonempty connected covering of a connected base is intrinsic for either of these two homology localizers exactly when it is isomorphic over the base to its identity covering. This assertion is specific to these coefficients; D.8 gives the contrary mod-$p$ behavior.

Here total asphericity means the condition of XII ms.~88 tested by all ordinary final images; we do not substitute the different diagonal-asphericity terminology used elsewhere in the literature. For a nonempty connected small category $A$, total $W_\infty$-asphericity is equivalent to every connected component of $\operatorname{El}_A(H)$ being weakly contractible, for every covariant $H:A\to\mathrm{Set}$. It is also equivalent to the same condition with integral acyclicity in place of weak contractibility. Exactness of $\colim_A:\Ab^A\to\Ab$ implies these conditions.

For a connected countable category $I$ without a weakly terminal object, and hence also in general, the implication from the universal ordinary-Cat-colimit comparison to filteredness remains unresolved here. F.4 gives a necessary totality condition and the full weakly-terminal case. The unbounded injective-ordinal examples do not refute this implication: the diagram $[n]\mapsto B\mathbb N^{n+1}$ has categorical colimit $B\mathbb N\simeq S^1$, whereas its Grothendieck construction has integral homology $\mathbb Z$ in every degree. On all of $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ its degree-$k$ fibre homology, for $k\geq1$, is the projective representable $\mathbb Z[\Delta_{\rm inj}([k-1],-)]$; the homotopy-colimit spectral sequence collapses. On an arbitrary unbounded full subcategory $A_S$, the restricted diagram need not be representable. Instead its higher derived colimits vanish by exactness in F.3, and its colimit is $\mathbb Z$: any two marked $k$-element ordered subsets admit embeddings into a common larger ordinal identifying their marks, then into an object of $A_S$. The categorical colimit is still $B\mathbb N$, since the same embeddings identify all coordinate generators and introduce precisely their commutative-monoid relation. Thus all these shapes fail the premise. This prevents importing the nonfiltered total example as an answer to the different Cat-colimit question.

Let $\mathcal C$ be either $\operatorname{Sp}_{\mathcal U}$ or $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with its indicated presentable infinity-category enhancement. We number the stages by \[ W_{\mathcal C}^{(0)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \mathcal C_1=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{I.9.1} \] Here $\mathcal S_W$ is the accessible reflective localization of spaces at exactly the class $W$, and $\mathbb D_{\mathcal E}(A)=\operatorname{Ho}\operatorname{Fun}(NA^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)$. The localizations in (I.9.1) exist and preserve finite products. Their constant-coefficient classes satisfy $W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}$. For every map $u:X\to Y$ of small spaces, \[ u\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xu\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}. \tag{I.9.2} \] The loop condition is tested at one basepoint in every component of $X$. Consequently \[ W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(1)} =W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(2)}=W_\infty, \tag{I.9.3} \] and \[ u\in W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_i(u)\text{ is an integral isomorphism for }i=1,2,\\ H_*(u\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p)\text{ is an isomorphism}. \end{cases} \tag{I.9.4} \] For a pointed connected component, $X\langle2\rangle$ means the homotopy fibre at its chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\leq2}X$. The map $u\langle2\rangle:X\langle2\rangle\to Y\langle2\rangle$ is induced by $u$ and the basepoints. The last two conditions of (I.9.4) are tested on every corresponding pointed component. There are no nilpotence or finite-type hypotheses. The second class is again accessible and product stable, so $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}}$ realizes it as an ordinary constant-coefficient class. This construction can be iterated at every finite stage for these two starting coefficients. It is a specified realization by localized spaces; functorial construction on all bare derivators and all exact morphisms remains the separate Open assertion of I.7.
